outline.chapter_title: Introduction to Mathematical Reasoning with Large Language Models
outline.description: Provides the motivation, challenges, and the landscape of mathematical reasoning for LLMs, introducing DeepSeekMath and its place among open‑source and closed models.
subtopics: Why mathematical reasoning is hard for language models
Historical progress: from early LLMs to GPT‑4, Gemini‑Ultra, and open‑source efforts
Overview of DeepSeekMath: goals and high‑level architecture
Key contributions of the DeepSeekMath paper

outline.chapter_title: Building a Large‑Scale Math Pre‑Training Corpus
outline.description: Explains how the DeepSeekMath Corpus was constructed from Common Crawl, including data selection, filtering, multilingual considerations, and de‑contamination.
subtopics: Seed data: OpenWebMath and its role
FastText classifier design and training procedure
Iterative data‑collection pipeline (four iterations)
Domain‑level heuristics and manual URL annotation
Deduplication, near‑deduplication, and token budgeting
Benchmark de‑contamination strategy
Multilingual coverage and its impact

outline.description: Describes experiments that compare the DeepSeekMath Corpus with existing math corpora, demonstrating its superiority in quality, scale, and multilinguality.
subtopics: Competing corpora: MathPile, OpenWebMath, Proof‑Pile‑2
Training protocol for 1.3B model on each corpus (150 B tokens)
Evaluation benchmarks (GSM8K, MATH, CMATH, etc.)
Analysis of learning curves and performance gaps
…Interpretation of results

outline.description: Details the architecture, data mixture, and training regimen used to produce the base model, followed by a thorough evaluation on math and general tasks.
subtopics: Model initialization from DeepSeek‑Coder‑Base‑v1.5
Token distribution (math, code, natural language)
Training hyperparameters (learning rate schedule, batch size)
Mathematical problem solving with chain‑of‑thought prompting
Program‑of‑thought (tool‑use) evaluation
Formal mathematics (miniF2F autoformalization)
General language understanding (MMLU), reasoning (BBH), coding (HumanEval/MBPP)
Ablation insights: code pre‑training vs. pure math pre‑training
